content:
alex: Heads-up — we've observed increased p99 on the hosted inference fleet since the scheduler tweak yesterday. Looks tied to continuous-batching queue delays.
maya: Which parameters changed? max_wait_ms or max_batch_tokens?
alex: max_wait_ms was increased from 4ms -> 8ms in the default policy to improve throughput. Also bumped global max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 8192 for some model families.
cheng: Any profiling data yet? p95/p99 numbers?
alex: Quick summary from last 6h canary vs prod:
```
canary (old): max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=4 -> p95=95ms, p99=260ms, throughput=880 tok/s
prod (new):  max_batch_tokens=8192, max_wait_ms=8 -> p95=120ms, p99=420ms, throughput=1000 tok/s
small-batch:  max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=2 -> p95=80ms,  p99=200ms, throughput=700 tok/s
```
Key: throughput up ~13% but p99 regressed badly.
sophie: Oof. Tail hit rates mostly for seq_len <512 or long ones?
alex: Tail dominated by a mix: short requests waiting behind large prefix-heavy batches (head-of-line blocking) + KV-cache misses that cause additional decoding latency. KV hit ratio dropped from 0.92 -> 0.86 in prod region.
lars: Kernel selection note: profiler shows attention kernel hot path switching to attention_kernel_v2 for long batches; v2 is faster for big batches but has worse single-request latency for small microbatches. We likely need dynamic kernel policy keyed by microbatch size and avg_seq_len.
perf-bot: Attached flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/1769001111
perf-bot: Top frames: attention_kernel_v2 (42%), kv_cache_lookup (18%), scheduler_enqueue_wait (12%)
maya: Can we tune scheduler to use smaller max_batch_tokens for routes with low KV hit or low seq_len? microbatch sizing per-route?
cheng: Yep — we already have per-model routing policies. We can add a conditional: if avg_seq_len_p50 < 512 -> max_batch_tokens = 4096 and max_wait_ms = 4. Otherwise keep higher batching.
alex: That should reduce H-O-L blocking. Also consider an early-flush threshold: if head_of_queue_wait > X ms then flush smaller batch.
sophie: Implementation idea: track first_request_enqueue_ts per batch, and expose max_head_wait_ms. If head wait > max_head_wait_ms, trigger immediate flush.
lars: Also a kernel selection override: prefer kernel_v3 for microbatch_count <= 8 or avg_seq_len < 600. v3 trades GPU occupancy for lower single-request latency.
maya: Any regressions recently in the kernel selector? We changed selection heuristics in commit 1f4ac2 last week.
alex: Yup — 1f4ac2 made selection bias towards high-throughput kernels when batch_tokens > 6000. That combined with larger max_batch_tokens caused worst-case combos.
infra-bot: CI perf test shows ~7% p99 increase for small-latency workloads on that branch: https://ci.redwood/build/1769
cheng: Short-term mitigation: rollback the max_wait_ms bump for sensitive routes and deploy kernel selector patch that considers microbatch_count.
alex: Do we have an AB test plan? I propose:
  - Roll back default max_wait_ms to 4ms for prod-critical routes (canary first)
  - Add per-route config: {max_batch_tokens, max_wait_ms, max_head_wait_ms}
  - Kernel selector: prefer kernel_v3 when microbatch_count <= 8 or avg_seq_len < 600
  - Add p99 alert at 2x baseline and trace sampling for tail requests

sophie: I'll add a draft rollout plan to the runbook. lmk if you want canary windows.
lars: Also add a KV-cache metric to the dashboard and set threshold alert (hit_ratio < 0.90) — many tails are correlated to KV misses.
maya: For experiments, suggest these CLI runs:
```
./run_bench --max_batch_tokens=4096 --max_wait_ms=4 --kv_cache=true --microbatch=8 --model=xlarge
./run_bench --max_batch_tokens=8192 --max_wait_ms=8 --kv_cache=false --microbatch=16 --model=xlarge
```
alex: I'll schedule the canary revert for 11:00 UTC and run the bench set after. If p99 drops to previous levels, we keep per-route higher batching as an opt-in only.
perf-bot: Noted. Creating issue PERF-1452 with stack traces and configs.
infra-bot: Canary deploy scheduled by ops: canary/2026-03-17-11:00
maya: One more: add histogram of batch sizes and microbatch counts to the console. That will make it easier to see where head-of-line blocking happens.
alex: Agreed. Action items: sophie runbook, cheng config patch + kernel selector PR, lars dashboard + alerts, maya bench + hist addition. I'll coordinate canary.
maya: :white_check_mark:
cheng: on it, will open PR with tests.
lars: I'll add KV hit panel and head_wait metric.
alex: Thanks team — let's target 24h to stabilize p99. If anyone sees an urgent spike post-change ping #oncall.
